records.title: Mirror section: Description and history
records.text: Section 1 Description and history Signature News is a mirror of the news kind of website: a website whose job is to publish current reports, grouped by subject and ordered by date, so a reader can see what is new and find reports on one subject. The news kind of website began as printed papers, then as lists of headlines with dates, and then as searchable archives. This mirror follows that same shape: headlines, subjects, dates, and a search over the reports. What this mirror reports is the network's own material. records.title: Mirror section: Math proof (standard math + metamath)
records.text: Section 2 Math proof (standard math + metamath) The mirror's filter rule is a deterministic function. For a query Q of words q1 … qn and a report R with a headline, a subject, and a body, the report matches when: match(Q, R) is true when every word of Q appears in R's headline, subject, or body Every matching report scores the same: the number of query words, which is the same for all matches of one query. records.title: Mirror section: Science proof
records.text: Section 3 Science proof The science behind this mirror is how reports are organized and found: by subject and by date. A reader who wants one subject reads that subject's reports; a reader who wants what is new reads by date. The mirror uses the simplest honest form of that idea: a fixed sample set of reports, each carrying a headline, a subject, a date, and a short body, with a filter that keeps only the reports carrying every word asked for. records.title: Mirror section: Spec / patent + 3D-print version
records.text: Section 5 Spec / patent + 3D-print version Spec. The Signature spec for this mirror is a draft specification for a news mirror over a fixed, network-owned report set: the report format (headline, subject, date, body), the filter rule from Section 2, the newest-first order rule, and the no-tracking, no-account design. The spec is a draft — ready to file, not filed, not a granted patent. 3D-print version. A news mirror is software: it has no physical form, so there is no 3D-print version of it. The mirror says so plainly rather than inventing one.
